# What Salesforce's Sales Cloud Agent Survey Says About Time Saved for Sellers

> **In short:** Salesforce says its Sales Cloud AI agents save sellers about six hours a week on non-selling tasks, according to a survey of 24 active customers. Sixty-three percent of those customers also report more accurate and complete CRM data.

If you have ever spent a Friday afternoon typing meeting notes into a database instead of talking to a customer, you know the feeling. Salesforce has released a new report on whether AI "sales agents" (software that takes on routine tasks on its own) are actually giving sales teams that time back. Here is what it found, and what it does and doesn't prove.

## What the company measured

Salesforce surveyed 24 customers who actively use the AI sales agents in its Sales Cloud product. Sales Cloud is the company's tool for managing sales work, and it includes a CRM (customer relationship management system, the place where teams store contacts, account details, and deal history). The survey ran online in late July 2026 and included 32 questions.

The company says the average seller spends about 60% of their time on tasks that aren't selling, like updating the CRM and researching accounts. That figure is Salesforce's own estimate, so treat it as its view rather than an independent measurement.

## The main findings, in plain terms

According to the report, these are the headline results:

- **Time back:** Sellers save an average of six hours a week. Customers who deployed agents for prospecting, account research, and pipeline management (the list of deals at each stage) reported saving five hours or more a week on those tasks.
- **Cleaner data:** 63% of customers say the agents give them more accurate and complete CRM data. Two in three say account research is more thorough.
- **Smoother deals:** Two in three customers report smoother handoffs between teams, and deals move 10% to 20% faster for two-thirds of account executives.
- **Revenue without hiring:** 57% of sales leaders agree agents let them grow revenue without adding headcount (the number of people on the team). Three in four say they kept their hiring plans the same while increasing sales output.

Keep in mind that 24 customers is a small group, and the survey only included people who already use the product. The results describe their experience. They don't prove what every team will get.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Even outside a sales job, the lesson applies. Repetitive admin work, like logging notes or looking things up, eats time that could go to the people you serve. Notice which of your own tasks feel like data entry.
- **For your business or work:** If your team uses a CRM, ask whether the notes and follow-ups are being captured consistently. The report's core claim is that better records lead to better forecasts, since a forecast (an estimate of future sales) is only as reliable as the data behind it.
- **If you're just getting started:** Read your company's sales tools documentation to see what automation is already switched on. You don't need to change anything to understand what's available.
- **If you already use it:** Compare the agent's logged activity with what your reps actually did for a week. Where they differ, you've found the gaps to review before you trust the forecast.

## Wrap-up

Salesforce's report suggests that AI agents can cut admin time for sellers and make CRM records more complete, at least for the customers it surveyed. The results come from the company itself and a small sample, so it's worth testing in your own team before drawing big conclusions. Your next step: this week, ask one seller how many hours of their week go to admin, and write down the answer as your baseline.
